reason: The commit consists of defensive null checks, a corrected stack-allocation size, and removal of redundant assignments. It introduces no new entry point, feature, configuration option, initialization requirement, API protocol, or input constraint. The existing fuzzers already drive the relevant high-level parsing, diagnostics, cleanup, and serialization paths using buffer, string, and file inputs, so no harness change is required to make the changed code reachable under its existing state model.
evidence: tidy_fuzzer invokes tidyParseBuffer, tidyCleanAndRepair, tidyRunDiagnostics, and tidySaveBuffer, covering parser, message-generation, cleanup, and output paths affected by the diff.
tidy_parse_string_fuzzer and tidy_xml_fuzzer exercise tidyParseString followed by cleanup, diagnostics, and serialization; tidy_parse_file_fuzzer and tidy_general_fuzzer also exercise tidyParseFile.
TY_(growStack) only changes TidyAlloc from new_capacity bytes to new_capacity * sizeof(Node**) bytes; its caller-facing behavior and input requirements are unchanged.
Changes in parser.c and message.c add checks such as parent &&, node->tag &&, html &&, n checks, and conditional element access; they do not add a distinct mode or required setup.
The fileio.c, messageobj.c, pprint.c, and streamio.c edits are internal correctness fixes with unchanged public APIs and no new harness-controlled state.
recommended_action: Keep the existing fuzz harnesses unchanged; no maintenance is justified by this source diff alone.
